## Natural history notes

A medium-sized dagger moth characterized by gray to brownish forewings with smeared dark markings and pale streaks that help it blend into bark and dead leaves. In Florida, it is found in forests, hammocks, wetlands, gardens, parks, roadsides, and other wooded or semi-open habitats with a variety of host plants. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the spiny, brightly marked caterpillars feed on many trees, shrubs, and herbaceous plants and can be irritating if handled.
